items.title: Author the thin-entrypoint contract migration execution plan
items.context: Document the target host-discovery architecture for Codex, Claude Code, and Antigravity/agy; distinguish entrypoints, canonical navigation, operational projection, and normative process facts; inventory hard-coded CLAUDE.md consumers; define shared registry migration, test-first rollout, compatibility and rollback, implementation Story slices, and the safe disposition of B-e514.

happy.desc: The execution-plan decision document exists and gives an implementable target architecture for Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, and Antigravity CLI (agy), separating host-discovery entrypoints, .lattice/Lattice.md navigation, the operational runbook projection, normative decision sources, and CLI/registry/gate mechanical authority; it also inventories current CLAUDE.md consumers and defines test-first sequencing, compatibility, rollback, implementation Story slices, and B-e514 convergence. WHY: proves the requested plan is complete enough to execute without inventing missing architecture during implementation.

edge.desc: The plan treats AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md size budgets as anti-regression ceilings rather than fill targets, preserves repository-local hard constraints such as the OMX ban without forcing them into universal generated templates, and does not propose CODEX.md or AGY.md as new host protocols. WHY: covers the boundary between shared generated assets, repository-local policy, and actual host discovery conventions.

The plan explicitly defines precedence and non-duplication across AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .lattice/Lattice.md, the runbook, normative decision docs, and mechanical registries/gates, including how Claude obtains shared rules without copying a second long root contract. WHY: prevents thin-entrypoint migration from creating a third drifting source of truth.

adversarial.desc: Cross-check the plan inventory against repository references to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and canonical-document path arrays; every behavior-affecting audit, docs-drift, reviewer, template, sync, trigger, managed-asset, and verifier consumer found is either assigned to a migration slice or explicitly justified out of scope. WHY: catches a cosmetically thin root document that leaves hidden Claude-first mechanical contracts active.

Challenge the rollout by simulating stale links, conflicting runbook commands, failed red tests, rollback after partial template migration, and B-e514 remaining blocked at TEST; the plan must specify fail-closed detection and a safe recovery/order of operations without declaring the old contract retired early. WHY: prevents an irreversible documentation cutover or false convergence when canonical consumers disagree.

items.userSees: User sees the heading "Proof-or-stop Thin Entrypoint Contract Migration Execution Plan" followed by an ordered implementation sequence, red/green verification matrix, rollback rules, and the B-e514 convergence decision.

verificationEvidence.command: rg -n "Proof-or-stop Thin Entrypoint Contract Migration Execution Plan" docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md docs/requirements/NAV.md
verificationEvidence.note: The exact heading and NAV entry exist; the hardened plan contains the target architecture, canonical registry, corrected dependency order, compatibility, rollback, failure exercises, and B-e514 convergence.
The plan rejects invented CODEX.md/AGY.md contracts, treats budgets as ceilings, and keeps OMX as repository-local user policy outside universal templates.

verificationEvidence.command: rg -n "Target hierarchy and precedence|Normative facts versus operational projection|Shared Canonical-Document Registry" docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md
verificationEvidence.note: Precedence and non-duplication are explicit across effective host entrypoints, .lattice navigation, the verified operational projection, normative decisions, and mechanical consumers.

The plan includes a real bounded tracked-text baseline: 600 hit lines across 134 files, classified 15 host-discovery / 511 migrate / 74 neutral-fixture with zero unclassified, plus named missing consumers and normative authority hits. It explicitly requires semantic reruns by successor Stories.

verificationEvidence.command: rg -n "Story 3 — Audit|Story 4 — Review|Story 5 — Active normative|Story 6 — Verifier|Story 7 — Init|Story 8 — B-e514|Story 9 — Legacy|Required failure exercises|Partial template migration|B-e514 remains in TEST" docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md
verificationEvidence.note: Consumers, normative authority and verifier readiness precede template thinning; the five concrete failure exercises specify fixture, expected failure, recovery and owner, and B-e514 remains the sole root owner.

items.title: Register the new execution plan in source-of-truth navigation
items.context: Update docs/requirements/NAV.md so the new active decision is discoverable and its declared file count remains accurate.

happy.desc: docs/requirements/NAV.md contains one discoverable entry for the new thin-entrypoint contract migration execution plan, points to the exact existing decision-document path, describes it as active normative planning authority, and its declared decision-file count equals an independent filesystem count under the navigation policy. WHY: proves the plan is reachable from the source-of-truth index and the index remains internally accurate.

edge.desc: The navigation update preserves ordering and surrounding entries, introduces no duplicate or case-variant link, and does not link to a legacy, retired, missing, or similarly named superseded document. WHY: covers ambiguous discovery when the requirements tree contains multiple root-document migration records.

adversarial.desc: Recompute the eligible decision-document count independently from NAV.md text and verify the declared count cannot pass merely because both the link and count were copied from a stale snapshot; also assert the new entry appears exactly once and resolves to the authored plan. WHY: catches self-consistent but factually stale navigation metadata.

Inspect the NAV diff for unrelated authority changes, accidental demotion of existing canonical documents, or wording that makes the operational runbook/root entrypoints co-equal normative sources. WHY: prevents a small indexing edit from silently changing source-of-truth precedence.

items.userSees: User sees "Proof-or-stop Thin Entrypoint Contract Migration Execution Plan" listed once in Source of Truth Navigation and the header count updated to "115 files".

verificationEvidence.note: Independent filesystem count returned 115, matching the NAV declaration; the exact active-authority link exists at NAV line 71.
The new path appears exactly once with the exact filename and is labeled active migration-planning authority, not implementation evidence.

verificationEvidence.command: rg -n "115 files|Proof-or-stop Thin Entrypoint Contract Migration Execution Plan" docs/requirements/NAV.md
verificationEvidence.note: NAV contains one count declaration and one matching plan entry; the linked target exists and the independent count is 115.
The product commit contains only NAV.md and the new decision document; surrounding authority entries were preserved and no implementation paths changed.

auditLog.reason: Address REVIEW findings F-001 through F-005 by correcting rollout order, adding normative-doc authority migration and retired-authority guards, completing consumer inventory, and specifying failure-scenario exercises.
Address F-006 and F-008 with semantic dual-read identity and an independently inspectable line-level scan manifest appendix.
